name: Handoff red-box at 50k/150k/300k/500k/700k/750k token-volume thresholds
description:
When session token usage crosses 50k, 150k, 300k, 500k, 700k, or 750k absolute tokens, fire an API-error-style red box recommending the operator request a handoff document. Each threshold fires at most once per session. Severity escalates with the threshold. Token counts come from the transcript JSONL via scripts/token_check.py — always available, no usage-meter dependency.
Migrated from percentage-based thresholds (33/50/75/90%) per operator directive 2026-05-03: "Address threshold, no longer percentages, thresholds are now token # gated." The free-radical biological metaphor — token accumulation is mitochondrial ROS buildup; sweeps are antioxidant clearance; absolute counts (not percentages) are the natural unit because ROS damage scales with molecule count, not fraction of cellular capacity.

absent_signal_fallback:
Token counts are always available via scripts/token_check.py reading
the transcript JSONL — no fallback needed. If token_check fails, the
hook surfaces a structured error rather than silently dropping.
why_high: Handoff quality drops as token volume climbs. 50k is early enough to capture comprehensive state before drift sets in; 500k/700k/750k escalate urgency so the operator never hits a cutoff without a written handoff in hand. Volume-based thresholds (vs percentage) ensure the rule fires reliably — there is no harness-level usage-meter dependency.
